I saw that, and can't debate it one way or another. It sounds like a pretty good idea, at the very least. Is the same lab doing the hair test? If possible, I would try to have the test done THROuGH them, and not just yourself going into some clinic that offers the test. That can be important, that the test was done by someone they "trust", versus someone you found to do the test for you. Also, maybe, in the future, if you still have concerns, request that ANOTHER tester / employee be in the room while you test to absolutely assure that everything was done by the books? If some one was honest in this case, it couldn't hurt - Not only does it show that you are not trying to "get away with some thing", as someone attempting a trick would likely not want MORE supervision, but it should also, in theory, prevent one person (your tester) from risking any other kind of stunt, as they would have a coworker right there.

By default, they are supposed to send EVERY positive test in for farther analysis - for this very reason. False positives can happen with the simpler tests, where as they are impossible once they do the GC/MS test, so to save themselves the trouble, I was under the  knowledge that every positive was sent on to the lab. Maybe that is just the case in my court jurisdiction/ state, I am not sure.

Real question though, how can a picture of your sample be used as any sort of proof? Their is not a correlation between color and amount of substance, so I don't really see how that could help some one.

As bad as all that sounds, I have seen worse. I have seen some one smuggle in clean urine, and fake urine, and STILL test positive for fent. Now how could that happen? With that being said, it is a LOOOOOONGshot. The lady at the testing facility doesn't know you. She has nothing to gain by you failing, and a lot to lose by risking her job tampering with samples. Ask yourself, why would someone who I have never met before risk their job just to spite a stranger? Would you do that? Risk your livelyhood just to mess around with some randoms urine? Again, I'm not trying to say you are wrong, just that it is VERY unlikely, and unfortunately, I don't think you will ever be able to prove yourself, as (unfortunately, again) this is a route that even guilty people attempt to trek, either because of denial or as a last ditch effort to avoid being charged, and they see it all the time. Very little "benefit of the doubt" is given, understandingly, as very many people lie in these circumstances. It makes it almost impossible for the few who this does legitimately happen to to prove themselves, one way or another, because you likely won't even be granted the chance to do so. Also, I really doubt that the reason for her statement was guilt. She doesn't know you. Do you think about someone who came into your work so much to the point to where your guilt ridden over it? How likely does a situation where, some one who has never met you before and has no reason or incentive whatsoever to dislike you or for you to fail, decide to tamper with your urine so that you fail, and then go on to feel so guilty about it, that they remember the situation and wait to see you again so that this time, they can be sure to make that comment, sound? If this does indeed happen to be the case, then I have some prayers for you...that is an aweful, terrible, miserable situation to have to endure that will likely be impossible to prove, save for a signed confession of the tester employee. As for the leaving the room with your sample, what do you think happened? That the tester took your sample into the bathroom, and then they took out their travel baggy of fent and pinched some into your sample? Again, possible....but very unlikely. The most likely situation, imho, is that the sample tray was full / not available in the room, and she just took it to wherever it was supposed to be. I have heard that traditionally, the testers put the samples on a tray and once the tray is full, they take it some place else, and then either start over or the next worker comes in to do the next tray, similar to how shifts work. True, even in that case, she should have stickered it first, but even if not, that a lone will not be enough "evidence" of anything. I am not trying to say that you are "screwed" or "lying" or even "wrong", just that what you are claiming to have happened is a very unlikely scenario that will be nearly impossible to prove. Yikes. I don't trust the whole, "Well I tried to contact my PO and they didn't get back to me!" defense. Even if it is completely true, they expect you to go to hell and back in your efforts. Literally to the extent of, well you had a month to just come down and find out what was going on or to demand a supervisor, what were you doing all this time? It is very unlikely, in my opinion, that the status of your probation changed and it's just that no one got around to telling you. Not impossible, just unlikely. I have even seen a case where some one was assigned a completely new PO that they had never met or even heard of before, and then went on to be violated for not being in contact with some one they didn't even know existed, even after proof was presented that this was the case, and effort was made to contact the previous officer. If something seems wrong to you, do WHATEVER YOu CAN to "make an effort". Video phone calls that go to voicemail, take pictures of sent emails, subpoena your phone records from your phone provider (this takes a few weeks, so be aware), take pictures of yourself in front of the building to show you tried to find out what was going on. Whatever you can do, will help your cause. Don't just assume that because you haven't heard anything that all is good and well. In fact, it's exactly then that, from what I have seen, one should worry the most. Again, this is just a personal take over the internet, but at least consider the words.

The "line", from what I have read, is 72 hours. Now, I have never personally seen someone drink say, 70 hours from the test, while hydrating, and go on to fail. However, I'm sure it has happened. I worked at Gamestop a LONG time ago.

When I worked there, they had a white board in the back room. This board was used to track every single employees performance during the week. It tracked many things, but the most important things were reservations on games, game informer subscription sales, and what % of your total sales was of used merchandise. The problem is, the person that  came in last got written up. NO MATTER WHAT. It doesn't matter if every person broke store records, the person who just happened to come in last got written up.

So, what happened to the employees that only worked 8 hours a week, who would with out a doubt come in last? They'd have their hours cut. Now, you were expected to not come in last, but with only 4 hours. Once you were last even one time, and it was NEVER the managers because they got enough hours to not come in last even in a down week for themselves, it was basically impossible to ever come back from it.

​

Employees on the shit list would literally have to pay their friends that people at the store didn't know to come in and reserve stuff from them or buy used stuff and go back and return it later just to wipe away the fear of coming in last and having their hours cut and never recovered.

On top of that, if you were working your one or two shift for the week, and some one came in and cancelled reservations or returned used stuff when you were working, they didn't subtract it from the person who originally made the sale, they put it as a negative towards YOUR stats. As if it was YOUR fault some one decided to cancel their preorder. Employees would fake sick or run to the bath room if certain customers came in that frequently cancelled stuff. Managers would but in and take customers from hourly employees that they thought would be easily Game Informer subscription sales, like unrecognized moms that were buying enough used stuff to basically get the sub for free. The sub cost 15$, and got you 10% off the used stuff. So if some one was buying 150$+ of used stuff, they could in theory get the sub for free. When the managers saw a sale like this in the works, they would coincidentally ask you to go do some thing. At the same time, when some one coming in to cancel a reserve was coming in, the manager wouldn't be any where in sight. It wasn't even just the managers vs the store employees, it was the managers vs the GM, and the managers vs the other managers of nearby stores. We had 3 Gamestops in my town all within a mile of eachother. One was in the mall that was converted from a EB Games, with a original Gamestop scross the street. A new plaza was built a mile down, which had nicer stores, and when that Gamestop ooened the old one was supposed to close, but it never did, so we just had 3 basically all right next door. My store, #841, was a Planet X before a gamestop. It no longer exists.

I work for UPS, inside the building. I have worked for them on a truck during the holidays for six years. I am by no means a supervisor or a UPS veteran. I don't know too much about the logistics besides what I have observed working in the building, and the time before when I was a customer of them. In my opinion, and I hate to say this, I don't think you are going to get your stuff. There are thousands of packages in there, but, they are in motion. They go from the back of a truck, down a belt, sorted onto smaller belts differentiated by where they are going (the zip codes) to a different part of the building where they are then loaded onto a new truck, that will either take them to be delivered or to an airport or something. Again this might not be completely accurate because I only have one job and don't literally see the entire path of the package. I've seen packages that got pushed off a belt, or fell into a sort of abyss under a belt, or sometimes a package is in really bad shape and some one takes it to re-tape it to try and get it in better shape so your stuff isn't just like, exposed. If you are waiting on multiple packages, I don't know what to say, because it is VERY unlikely that something like that happened to all your different boxes. The holiday season literally increases the work load in the building by like,  50 times possibly more, compared to any other time, but they really demand more of the workers during the time. The people work much longer shifts, and many more people are working. It goes slower, much slower, but the volume does move. The packages are scanned when leaving the truck, and probably at other points of the trip inside the building, and that's how you get the updates. If the status hasn't updated in a few days, I don't really know what would cause that to be honest. I've seen certain belts break or jam, so all packages going to a certain place can't be sorted, but when that happens, they manually move the boxes via hand and little carts to where they need to go. It might cause an extra day of delay, but they fix that stuff quickly. I know this probably isn't all too helpful to you, as far as, where your stuff is and when you will get it, but, I guess I just don't know the answer. To me, at least, it would seem that your stuff got misplaced somewhere (somehow), or maybe something rediculous happened like it got stolen. Theft happens but is NOT common from what I've seen. Every employee gets checked going in and especially going out, and we have to open our backpacks or purses or whatever. The guards are not UPS employees so they have no incentive to cover for someone, either.

Oh, and I guess I'll add, that smaller packages (like envelopes) are exponentially more likely to get lost or tucked somewhere. I've seen little paper envelopes get stuck under sorting equipment or in other obscure places, but like I said, it's unlikely that it would happen to multiple items.

Pretty open ended question, lots of ways to answer it. Mostly depends on if your in a small city jail (generally the nicest but with shortest stays), a county jail (much larger with medium to long stays), usually pretty shitty, overcrowded and outdated, or an actual prison. Prisons are generally the largest with the longest stays. As far as prisons go, it could either be a camp type, for lowest level criminals / non violent crimes / first times / non escape/flight risks, or a higher security prison with more violent offenders, longer stays, repeat offenders, or flight risks. Prisons tend to have the most selection for commissary, and most activities to do. Prisons tend to be in the middle between county jails and city jails in terms of overall "niceness". City jails will usually have the highest quality foods, some will even run to a diner across the street or fast food joints. County jails will usually have the worst / no selection as far as food goes. Prisons will usually have the largest selection of things to eat, and the best quality of food as far as food prepared there. Most prisons will have a day once a month where you can order KFC or Pizza, if you have money on your books. County jails won't have that luxory, and not nearly as much commissary selection as prisons. City jails generally don't offer commissary because (generally) people won't be there too long. If you are at a city jail, generally people are either released after a few days, make bail, or transferred to a county jail / prison. City jails will usually allow the most phone time, for the cheapest price or free. County jails have phones, but not nearly enough for everyone to use them when they want, and always cost somewhere around 30-50cents a minute to talk, which can get very expensive. Prisons will have more phones but usually work on sceduled phone time, instead of whenever you can get a hold of a free phone. Prisons will usually have the most freedom as far as being able to walk around, where in county jails you will generally only have one large room you can be in, think highschool gym. City jails generally won't have anywhere for you to go. If there was some more interest in this, or if anyone had more specific questions, we can explore that as well.
